title: View bytes as decimal or octal
description:
An attempt at implementing request in issue #18615. Adding octal view
while at it, in case anybody happens to prefer that or compare with
reference data in octal.

Both decimal and octal view have three byte wide columns, which is
visually distinctive from hex view. Decimal uses leading spaces, which
makes it clearly different from octal view.

Some ternary operators previously done based on BYTES_HEX are now using
BYTES_BITS. This change is done as the new BYTES_DEC and BYTES_OCT have
more in common with BYTES_HEX and are either equivalent in context or
closer linked to BYTES_HEX (e.g. for calculating column widths).

While translations should be updated, I am unsure if this is automated.
Also, if attempted, lupdate picks up changes from unrelated commits.

Closes #18615

notes.body: This change of value (of BYTES_BITS) will cause a problem reading existing recent files.

  • 4b6b67ab...b911cf28 - 3 commits from branch wireshark:master
  • 0cc89260 - View bytes as decimal or octal
[Compare with previous version](/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/10022/diffs?diff_id=625756383&start_sha=4b6b67abc59cfee0a182141db3da7192c1803c82)

I have reworked the patch to not change the enum order and handling the values in current enum order. Options are still shown in menus in hex/dec/oct/bits order.

BTW, just for my curiosity, would the recent file not be written and read based on the value/string pairs in bytes_view_type_values?

I think this calculation is a bit magic, it doesn't clearly show how chars_per_byte is calculated.
I would like explicit values for each view type.

changed this line in [version 3 of the diff](/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/10022/diffs?diff_id=628262268&start_sha=0cc8926072e8c86df6216f47d8595a0ab2d4116c#01d92a28aff6fba2044b8c9548f6f6dd77095502_122_121)

I have reworked to expand the ternary to a switch statements when doing such magic.

In cases where the single exception is BYTES_BITS, I have left the ternary in place.
I hope that's still OK - otherwise ByteViewText::ByteViewText() initialisation needs quite the ternary combo, I think.
